MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN
NORTH SUMATRA PROVINCE
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN CITY NUMBER 3 OF 2021
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, thus requiring regulation as the basis for implementing comprehensive and integrated protection of women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City; In View of:

1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1984 Number 29, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3277); 3. Law Number 5 of 1998 concerning Ratification of the Convention Against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1998 Number 164, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3783); 4. Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 165, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3886); 5. Law Number 4 of 2001 concerning Establishment of Padang Sidempuan City (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 84 of 2001, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4111); 6. Law Number 20 of 2003 concerning National Education System (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2003 Number 78, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4301); 7. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4844); 8. Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2007 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4720); 9. Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 244, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5587) as amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2015 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5679); 10. Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning Stipulation of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law Number 1 of 2016 concerning Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection into Law (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2016 Number 237, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5946); 11. Government Regulation Number 10 of 1983 concerning Marriage and Divorce Permits for Civil Servants (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1983 Number 13, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3250) as amended by Government Regulation Number 45 of 1990 concerning Amendment to Government Regulation Number 10 of 1983 concerning Marriage and Divorce Permits for Civil Servants (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1990 Number 61, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3424); 12. Government Regulation Number 4 of 2006 concerning Implementation and Cooperation for Recovery of Victims of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2006 Number 15, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4604); 13. Government Regulation Number 38 of 2007 concerning Division of Government Affairs Between the Government, Provincial Regional Government and Regency/City Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2007 Number 82, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4737); 14. Presidential Instruction Number 5 of 2014 concerning National Movement Against Sexual Crimes Against Children; 15. Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 1 of 2010 concerning Minimum Service Standards for Integrated Services for Women and Child Victims of Violence; 16. Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 1 of 2011 concerning Guidelines for Evaluation of Child-Friendly Regencies/Cities; 17. Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 11 of 2011 concerning Policy for Development of Child-Friendly Regencies/Cities; 18. Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 12 of 2011 concerning Indicators of Child-Friendly Regencies/Cities; 19. Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 13 of 2011 concerning Guidelines for Development of Child-Friendly Regencies/Cities; 20.

CHAPTER VI
FORMS OF VIOLENCE
Article 10
Forms of violence include:
a. physical violence;
b. psychological violence;
c. sexual violence; and/or
d. domestic neglect.

Article 8
The family, in the effort to protect the rights of women, is obligated to:
a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political, and cultural affairs; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations of the rights of women in the household.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Padang Sidempuan. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Mayor is the Mayor of Padang Sidempuan. 5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD of Padang Sidempuan City is a Regional People's Representative Institution positioned as an element of Regional Government Administration. 6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in administering governmental affairs that are the authority of the region. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 8. Women Empowerment and Child Protection System is the entire process of implementing women empowerment and child protection carried out comprehensively, inclusively, and integratively starting from the stage of report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, up to repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of crime and violence to their social environment. 9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 11. Victim is a person who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that causes injury or death to another person or causes physical damage or damage to another person's property. 13. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Violence against children is any action that results or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children and among people who are their dependents. 18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from a regional area to their area of origin. 20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 21. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of violence victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 24. Child Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 25. Child friendly city task force hereinafter abbreviated as KLA task force is a coordinative institution at the city level that coordinates policies, programs and activities to realize KLA. 26. Business Entity is an institution that daily carries out activities seeking profit and gain, but has a commitment to the protection of women and children. 27. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so they can carry out their social functions. 28. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development program policies. 29.

Article 13
Sexual violence as referred to in Article 10 letter c in the form of:
a. acts of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
c. coercion of sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Article 11
Physical violence as referred to in Article 10 letter a results in:
a. the victim falling ill or being seriously injured;
b. the death of the victim; and
c. causing illness or impediment to carrying out work duties or livelihood or daily activities.

CHAPTER XVI
COOPERATION
Article 45
(1) Regional cooperation is joint efforts between regions with other regions, between regions and third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on the balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.
(2) Regional cooperation with third parties, hereinafter abbreviated as KSDPK, is joint efforts undertaken by regions with third parties in the context of implementing governmental affairs that are regional authority to improve community welfare and accelerate the fulfillment of public services.
(3) In order to achieve the objective of protecting the rights of women and children from acts of violence, regional governments cooperate with:
a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions
(4) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) includes:
a. exchange of data and information
b. rehabilitation of victims of acts of violence
c. repatriation and social reintegration, and
d. provision of physical evidence and witnesses which are followed up in accordance with applicable law.

Article 7
(1) Obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
(2) The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) are based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.
(3) The obligations and responsibilities of the community towards child protection are implemented through community role activities in the implementation of child protection.
(4) The obligations and responsibilities of the community towards child protection are implemented through community role activities in the implementation of child protection.
(5) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (4) are implemented by involving community organizations, academics, and child welfare observers.

Article 18
(1) Health Services are carried out by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is carried out by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual guides by providing counseling, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of the victim.
(3) Provision of counseling is carried out by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guides by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
(5) Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can return to carrying out their social functions in society.

CHAPTER XVIII
CRIMINAL PROVISIONS
Article 48
Every person who commits a criminal act/violence as referred to in Article 11, Article 12, Article 13, and Article 14 shall be subject to criminal punishment in accordance with the provisions of the prevailing laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IX
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
2021, No. 3 -84-

CHAPTER XII
INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Article 30
In the context of implementing the Protection of Women and Children, the following shall be established:
a. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A);
b. Family Welfare Consultation Institution; and
c. Other institutions in accordance with needs and/or provisions of laws and regulations.

Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so they can carry out their social functions. 28. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development program policies. 29.

(2) Gender and Children Data System is the institutionalization of gender and children data administration consisting of components-components-components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/agencies and regions in the framework of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that is gender responsive and child sensitive.
(3) Gender Data is data regarding relational relationships in status, roles and conditions between men and women.
(4) Disaggregated Data is data disaggregated by sex, age, status and conditions of women in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, political field and decision making, legal and socio-cultural fields and violence.
(5) Types of gender and children data:
a. gender data:
1. gender data in economic field including among others gender issues in labor, KUKM, industry and trade, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and marine affairs, transportation, science and technology and infrastructure;
2. gender data in political, social and legal fields;
3. women's rights protection data; and
4. family welfare and resilience development data.
b. children data:
1. civil rights and freedoms;
2. family environment and alternative care;
3. basic health and welfare;
4. education, leisure time utilization and cultural activities; and
5. special protection.
(6) Gender analysis is a process of analyzing disaggregated data by sex conducted systematically with the purpose of identifying gender issues and factors that can influence development, particularly related to gender equality issues which are the objective of development.

CHAPTER XVI
COOPERATION
Article 45
(1) Regional cooperation is joint efforts between regions with other regions, between regions and third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on the balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.
(2) Regional cooperation with third parties, hereinafter abbreviated as KSDPK, is joint efforts undertaken by regions with third parties in the context of implementing governmental affairs that are regional authority to improve community welfare and accelerate the fulfillment of public services.
(3) In order to achieve the objective of protecting the rights of women and children from acts of violence, regional governments cooperate with:
a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions
(4) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) includes:
a. exchange of data and information
b. rehabilitation of victims of acts of violence
c. repatriation and social reintegration, and
d. provision of physical evidence and witnesses which are followed up in accordance with applicable law.

CHAPTER XV
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 44
(1) The community may participate in the implementation of women's empowerment activities.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, community groups and community organizations.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
    a. cooperation;
    b. an active role in policy formulation; and
    c. complaints/reports.
(4) The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by a Mayor's Regulation.

Article 27
(1) Every person, community institution, university and business entity has the right to utilize the women and children data information system of Padang Sidempuan City by citing the data.
(2) Every person, community institution, university and business entity may partner as a provider or user of gender and child-related data and information to the administrator of the women and children data information system of Padang Sidempuan City for subsequent verification, data entry, and publication.

Article 35
(1) The Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection (P2TP2A) at City Level shall be established based on a Mayor's Decree and a District Head's Decree for the sub-district level.
(2) Membership of the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A) may consist of elements from regional apparatus, professional organizations, academics, community leaders and other elements as needed.
(3) Further provisions regarding P2TP2A shall be regulated by a Mayor Regulation.

Article 41
(1) To make effective the development of the Child-Friendly City (Kota Layak Anak), a Child-Friendly City (Kota Layak Anak) Task Force shall be established as determined by the Mayor's Decree.
(2) Membership of the Child-Friendly City (Kota Layak Anak) Task Force may come from the Regional Government, child representatives, the business sector, religious leaders, community leaders, and other parties as needed.

Article 18
(1) Health Services are carried out by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is carried out by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual guides by providing counseling, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of the victim.
(3) Provision of counseling is carried out by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guides by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
(5) Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can return to carrying out their social functions in society.

Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the regional government or community-based, which includes: referral center, business consultation center, reproductive health consultation center, legal consultation center, integrated crisis center (PKT), integrated service center (PPT), trauma recovery center (trauma center), women crisis center, training center, science and technology information center (PIPTEK), safe house (shelter), transit house, children's friend telephone (TESA) 129, or other forms.

CHAPTER XI
CHILDREN'S FORUM
Article 28
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to establish a children's forum at the Padang Sidempuan City level as participation through the children's forum.
(2) The children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) constitutes a representation of children, both representation of children's geographical domicile, components of children's socio-cultural groups and children's educational background as well as accommodating the interests of children with special needs.
(3) In every formulation of policies related to children, the Regional Government must consider and accommodate the opinions of children conveyed through the children's forum.
(4) The establishment of the children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Mayor's Decree.
(5) Sources of financing for the implementation of children's forum activities may come from:
a. contributions from members of the children's forum;
b. donations from the community/private parties that are legal and non-binding in nature;
c. assistance from the City Government; and/or
d. other sources of financing in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 7
(1) Obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
(2) The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) are based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.
(3) The obligations and responsibilities of the community towards child protection are implemented through community role activities in the implementation of child protection.
(4) The obligations and responsibilities of the community towards child protection are implemented through community role activities in the implementation of child protection.
(5) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (4) are implemented by involving community organizations, academics, and child welfare observers.

(2) To increase the availability and utilization of gender and child data and information in the formulation, planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of development programs/activities.

 b. establish or strengthen coordination mechanisms among ministries/agencies and regions in the implementation of disaggregated data collection;
 c. increase the availability and utilization of disaggregated data for planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting of results of gender-responsive and child-sensitive development policies/programs/activities in ministries/agencies and regions.

 b. agencies domiciled in Padang Sidempuan City; and
 c. the general public/public.

Article 37
To guarantee the fulfillment of children's rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination, real integrated efforts are needed between the Regional Government, community and business sector through the development of Child-Friendly Cities.

Article 23
(1) Gender Mainstreaming or abbreviated as PUG is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and gender justice in a number of aspects of human life (household, society and State), through policies and programs that take into account the experiences and aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies in various aspects of life and development.
(2) In an effort to accelerate the institutionalization of gender mainstreaming in all SKPD, a PUG Working Group is established.
(3) Members of the PUG Working Group are all heads/leaders of SKPD.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

Considering:

CONCERNING

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, thus requiring regulation as the basis for implementing comprehensive and integrated protection of women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City; In View of:

COOPERATION
Article 45
(1) Regional cooperation is joint efforts between regions with other regions, between regions and third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on the balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.
(2) Regional cooperation with third parties, hereinafter abbreviated as KSDPK, is joint efforts undertaken by regions with third parties in the context of implementing governmental affairs that are regional authority to improve community welfare and accelerate the fulfillment of public services.

a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions
(4) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) includes:
a. exchange of data and information
b. rehabilitation of victims of acts of violence
c. repatriation and social reintegration, and
d. provision of physical evidence and witnesses which are followed up in accordance with applicable law.

Article 18
(1) Health Services are carried out by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is carried out by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual guides by providing counseling, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of the victim.
(3) Provision of counseling is carried out by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guides by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
(5) Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can return to carrying out their social functions in society.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, thus requiring regulation as the basis for implementing comprehensive and integrated protection of women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City; In View of:

Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so they can carry out their social functions. 28. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development program policies. 29.

CHILDREN'S FORUM
Article 28
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to establish a children's forum at the Padang Sidempuan City level as participation through the children's forum.

Article 18
(1) Health Services are carried out by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is carried out by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual guides by providing counseling, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of the victim.
(3) Provision of counseling is carried out by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guides by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.

CHAPTER XVI
COOPERATION
Article 45
(1) Regional cooperation is joint efforts between regions with other regions, between regions and third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on the balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.
(2) Regional cooperation with third parties, hereinafter abbreviated as KSDPK, is joint efforts undertaken by regions with third parties in the context of implementing governmental affairs that are regional authority to improve community welfare and accelerate the fulfillment of public services.
(3) In order to achieve the objective of protecting the rights of women and children from acts of violence, regional governments cooperate with:
a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions
(4) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) includes:
a. exchange of data and information
b. rehabilitation of victims of acts of violence
c. repatriation and social reintegration, and
d. provision of physical evidence and witnesses which are followed up in accordance with applicable law.

Article 13
Sexual violence as referred to in Article 10 letter c in the form of:
a. acts of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
c. coercion of sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

CHAPTER VI
FORMS OF VIOLENCE
Article 10
Forms of violence include:
a. physical violence;
b. psychological violence;
c. sexual violence; and/or
d. domestic neglect.

Article 11
Physical violence as referred to in Article 10 letter a results in:
a. the victim falling ill or being seriously injured;
b. the death of the victim; and
c. causing illness or impediment to carrying out work duties or livelihood or daily activities.

Article 37
To guarantee the fulfillment of children's rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination, real integrated efforts are needed between the Regional Government, community and business sector through the development of Child-Friendly Cities.

Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the regional government or community-based, which includes: referral center, business consultation center, reproductive health consultation center, legal consultation center, integrated crisis center (PKT), integrated service center (PPT), trauma recovery center (trauma center), women crisis center, training center, science and technology information center (PIPTEK), safe house (shelter), transit house, children's friend telephone (TESA) 129, or other forms.

Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of violence victims. 23. Child Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 25. Child friendly city task force hereinafter abbreviated as KLA task force is a coordinative institution at the city level that coordinates policies, programs and activities to realize KLA. 26. Business Entity is an institution that daily carries out activities seeking profit and gain, but has a commitment to the protection of women and children. 27. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so they can carry out their social functions. 28. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development program policies. 29.

Violence is any act that causes injury or death to another person or causes physical damage or damage to another person's property. 13. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Violence against children is any action that results or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 15. CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Padang Sidempuan. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Mayor is the Mayor of Padang Sidempuan. 5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD of Padang Sidempuan City is a Regional People's Representative Institution positioned as an element of Regional Government Administration. 6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in administering governmental affairs that are the authority of the region. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 8. Women Empowerment and Child Protection System is the entire process of implementing women empowerment and child protection carried out comprehensively, inclusively, and integratively starting from the stage of report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, up to repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of crime and violence to their social environment. 9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 11. Victim is a person who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that causes injury or death to another person or causes physical damage or damage to another person's property. 13. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Violence against children is any action that results or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children and among people who are their dependents. 18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from a regional area to their area of origin. 20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 21. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of violence victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 24. Child Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 25. Child friendly city task force hereinafter abbreviated as KLA task force is a coordinative institution at the city level that coordinates policies, programs and activities to realize KLA. 26. Business Entity is an institution that daily carries out activities seeking profit and gain, but has a commitment to the protection of women and children. 27. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so they can carry out their social functions. 28. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development program policies. 29.

Article 8
The family, in the effort to protect the rights of women, is obligated to:
a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political, and cultural affairs; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations of the rights of women in the household.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Padang Sidempuan. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Mayor is the Mayor of Padang Sidempuan. 5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD of Padang Sidempuan City is a Regional People's Representative Institution positioned as an element of Regional Government Administration. 6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in administering governmental affairs that are the authority of the region. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 8. Women Empowerment and Child Protection System is the entire process of implementing women empowerment and child protection carried out comprehensively, inclusively, and integratively starting from the stage of report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, up to repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of crime and violence to their social environment. 9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 11. Victim is a person who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that causes injury or death to another person or causes physical damage or damage to another person's property. 13. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Violence against children is any action that results or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children and among people who are their dependents. 18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from a regional area to their area of origin. 20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 21. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of violence victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 24. Child Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 25. Child friendly city task force hereinafter abbreviated as KLA task force is a coordinative institution at the city level that coordinates policies, programs and activities to realize KLA. 26. Business Entity is an institution that daily carries out activities seeking profit and gain, but has a commitment to the protection of women and children. 27. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so they can carry out their social functions. 28. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development program policies. 29.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN CITY NUMBER 3 OF 2021
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, thus requiring regulation as the basis for implementing comprehensive and integrated protection of women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City; In View of:

1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Article 23
(1) Gender Mainstreaming or abbreviated as PUG is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and gender justice in a number of aspects of human life (household, society and State), through policies and programs that take into account the experiences and aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies in various aspects of life and development.

COOPERATION
Article 45
(1) Regional cooperation is joint efforts between regions with other regions, between regions and third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on the balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.

b. regencies/cities; and

Article 20
(1) Information system is a system to collect, prepare, store, process, analyze and/or disseminate information.
(2) Gender and Children Data System is the institutionalization of gender and children data administration consisting of components-components-components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/agencies and regions in the framework of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that is gender responsive and child sensitive.
(3) Gender Data is data regarding relational relationships in status, roles and conditions between men and women.
(4) Disaggregated Data is data disaggregated by sex, age, status and conditions of women in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, political field and decision making, legal and socio-cultural fields and violence.
(5) Types of gender and children data:
a. gender data:
1. gender data in economic field including among others gender issues in labor, KUKM, industry and trade, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and marine affairs, transportation, science and technology and infrastructure;
2. gender data in political, social and legal fields;
3. women's rights protection data; and
4. family welfare and resilience development data.
b. children data:
1. civil rights and freedoms;
2. family environment and alternative care;
3. basic health and welfare;
4. education, leisure time utilization and cultural activities; and
5. special protection.
(6) Gender analysis is a process of analyzing disaggregated data by sex conducted systematically with the purpose of identifying gender issues and factors that can influence development, particularly related to gender equality issues which are the objective of development.

FUNDING

(1) Regional Governments are obligated to provide budget for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs and activities.

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD); and
b. other legal and non-binding sources based on the provisions of laws and regulations.

FORMS OF VIOLENCE
Article 10
Forms of violence include:
a. physical violence;
b. psychological violence;
c. sexual violence; and/or
d. domestic neglect.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Padang Sidempuan. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Mayor is the Mayor of Padang Sidempuan. 5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD of Padang Sidempuan City is a Regional People's Representative Institution positioned as an element of Regional Government Administration. 6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in administering governmental affairs that are the authority of the region. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 8. Women Empowerment and Child Protection System is the entire process of implementing women empowerment and child protection carried out comprehensively, inclusively, and integratively starting from the stage of report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, up to repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of crime and violence to their social environment. 9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 11. Victim is a person who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that causes injury or death to another person or causes physical damage or damage to another person's property. 13. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Violence against children is any action that results or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children and among people who are their dependents. 18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from a regional area to their area of origin. 20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 21. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of violence victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 24. Child Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 25. Child friendly city task force hereinafter abbreviated as KLA task force is a coordinative institution at the city level that coordinates policies, programs and activities to realize KLA. 26. Business Entity is an institution that daily carries out activities seeking profit and gain, but has a commitment to the protection of women and children. 27. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so they can carry out their social functions. 28. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development program policies. 29.

CHAPTER XVI
COOPERATION
Article 45
(1) Regional cooperation is joint efforts between regions with other regions, between regions and third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on the balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.
(2) Regional cooperation with third parties, hereinafter abbreviated as KSDPK, is joint efforts undertaken by regions with third parties in the context of implementing governmental affairs that are regional authority to improve community welfare and accelerate the fulfillment of public services.
(3) In order to achieve the objective of protecting the rights of women and children from acts of violence, regional governments cooperate with:
a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions
(4) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) includes:
a. exchange of data and information
b. rehabilitation of victims of acts of violence
c. repatriation and social reintegration, and
d. provision of physical evidence and witnesses which are followed up in accordance with applicable law.

CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, thus requiring regulation as the basis for implementing comprehensive and integrated protection of women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City; In View of:

Article 7
(1) Obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of women and children;

(2) The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) are based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

BABX
INFORMATION SYSTEM FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN DATA
Article 20
(1) Information system is a system to collect, prepare, store, process, analyze and/or disseminate information.
(2) Gender and Children Data System is the institutionalization of gender and children data administration consisting of components-components-components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/agencies and regions in the framework of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that is gender responsive and child sensitive.
(3) Gender Data is data regarding relational relationships in status, roles and conditions between men and women.
(4) Disaggregated Data is data disaggregated by sex, age, status and conditions of women in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, political field and decision making, legal and socio-cultural fields and violence.
(5) Types of gender and children data:
a. gender data:
1. gender data in economic field including among others gender issues in labor, KUKM, industry and trade, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and marine affairs, transportation, science and technology and infrastructure;
2. gender data in political, social and legal fields;
3. women's rights protection data; and
4. family welfare and resilience development data.
b. children data:
1. civil rights and freedoms;
2. family environment and alternative care;
3. basic health and welfare;
4. education, leisure time utilization and cultural activities; and
5. special protection.
(6) Gender analysis is a process of analyzing disaggregated data by sex conducted systematically with the purpose of identifying gender issues and factors that can influence development, particularly related to gender equality issues which are the objective of development.

(2) Victim assistance is carried out by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual guides by providing counseling, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of the victim.
(3) Provision of counseling is carried out by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guides by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
(5) Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can return to carrying out their social functions in society.

Article 45

a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions

a. exchange of data and information

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, thus requiring regulation as the basis for implementing comprehensive and integrated protection of women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City; In View of:

INFORMATION SYSTEM FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN DATA
Article 20
(1) Information system is a system to collect, prepare, store, process, analyze and/or disseminate information.
(2) Gender and Children Data System is the institutionalization of gender and children data administration consisting of components-components-components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/agencies and regions in the framework of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that is gender responsive and child sensitive.
(3) Gender Data is data regarding relational relationships in status, roles and conditions between men and women.
(4) Disaggregated Data is data disaggregated by sex, age, status and conditions of women in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, political field and decision making, legal and socio-cultural fields and violence.
(5) Types of gender and children data:
a. gender data:
1. gender data in economic field including among others gender issues in labor, KUKM, industry and trade, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and marine affairs, transportation, science and technology and infrastructure;
2. gender data in political, social and legal fields;
3. women's rights protection data; and
4. family welfare and resilience development data.
b. children data:
1. civil rights and freedoms;
2. family environment and alternative care;
3. basic health and welfare;
4. education, leisure time utilization and cultural activities; and
5. special protection.
(6) Gender analysis is a process of analyzing disaggregated data by sex conducted systematically with the purpose of identifying gender issues and factors that can influence development, particularly related to gender equality issues which are the objective of development.

Article 23
(1) Gender Mainstreaming or abbreviated as PUG is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and gender justice in a number of aspects of human life (household, society and State), through policies and programs that take into account the experiences and aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies in various aspects of life and development.

(3) Members of the PUG Working Group are all heads/leaders of SKPD.

(4) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) includes:

Article 18
(1) Health Services are carried out by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
(2) Victim assistance is carried out by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual guides by providing counseling, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and self-recovery of the victim.
(3) Provision of counseling is carried out by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
(4) Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guides by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN CITY NUMBER 3 OF 2021
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creatures of Almighty God who have human rights guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, therefore women and children must be protected from all forms of violence and discrimination; b. that violence against women and children in the Region tends to increase, therefore the Regional Government and/or community need to play an active role optimally to provide protection, so that women and children are prevented and free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth; c. that protection of women and children is a mandatory concurrent affair which is the authority, obligation, and responsibility of the Regional Government, thus requiring regulation as the basis for implementing comprehensive and integrated protection of women and children; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City; In View of:

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Padang Sidempuan. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Victim is a person who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that causes injury or death to another person or causes physical damage or damage to another person's property. 13. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Violence against children is any action that results or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 15. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so they can carry out their social functions. 28. Article 20
(1) Information system is a system to collect, prepare, store, process, analyze and/or disseminate information.
(2) Gender and Children Data System is the institutionalization of gender and children data administration consisting of components-components-components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/agencies and regions in the framework of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of development that is gender responsive and child sensitive.
(3) Gender Data is data regarding relational relationships in status, roles and conditions between men and women.
(4) Disaggregated Data is data disaggregated by sex, age, status and conditions of women in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, political field and decision making, legal and socio-cultural fields and violence.
(5) Types of gender and children data:
a. gender data:
1. gender data in economic field including among others gender issues in labor, KUKM, industry and trade, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and marine affairs, transportation, science and technology and infrastructure;
2. gender data in political, social and legal fields;
3. women's rights protection data; and
4. family welfare and resilience development data.
b. children data:
1. civil rights and freedoms;
2. family environment and alternative care;
3. basic health and welfare;
4. education, leisure time utilization and cultural activities; and
5. special protection.
(6) Gender analysis is a process of analyzing disaggregated data by sex conducted systematically with the purpose of identifying gender issues and factors that can influence development, particularly related to gender equality issues which are the objective of development.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Padang Sidempuan. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Mayor is the Mayor of Padang Sidempuan. 5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD of Padang Sidempuan City is a Regional People's Representative Institution positioned as an element of Regional Government Administration. 6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in administering governmental affairs that are the authority of the region. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 8. Women Empowerment and Child Protection System is the entire process of implementing women empowerment and child protection carried out comprehensively, inclusively, and integratively starting from the stage of report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, up to repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of crime and violence to their social environment. 9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 11. Victim is a person who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that causes injury or death to another person or causes physical damage or damage to another person's property. 13. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 14. Violence against children is any action that results or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children and among people who are their dependents. 18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from a regional area to their area of origin. 20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 21. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of violence victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 24. Child Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 25. Child friendly city task force hereinafter abbreviated as KLA task force is a coordinative institution at the city level that coordinates policies, programs and activities to realize KLA. 26. Business Entity is an institution that daily carries out activities seeking profit and gain, but has a commitment to the protection of women and children. 27. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so they can carry out their social functions. 28. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development program policies. 29.
